title: Second Place Marrow
mood: raw, rueful and funny at her own expense
subject: a woman losing the village show's biggest-marrow prize to the same retired man for the third summer running, with her allotment marrow on a wheelbarrow
caption: UK pop-soul rock in the raw 2025 London confessional style. Loose live drums with a heavy tom fill into each chorus; an upright piano hammered in block chords; a crunchy overdriven electric guitar strumming whole bars; a simple root-note bass guitar. Raw and close production, slight room bleed, the voice very forward and unpolished. Female voice, a raspy chest belt, talk-singing the verses and cracking into a shouted chorus. 76 BPM, F major. Raw, rueful and funny at her own expense. No autotune, no trap beat, no EDM build, no glossy pop polish, no choir.
lyrics:
[Intro - overdriven guitar and kick drum]

[Verse 1]
I fed it tea and banana skins all summer
Talked to it nightly like it was my son
Wheeled it to the village hall in a barrow
Twelve kilos of hope under a tea towel

[Pre-Chorus]
And there's Derek at the trestle table
Smiling like he knows

[Chorus]
Second place marrow, second place me
Red rosette for Derek, blue one for me
Three summers running and the judge didn't blink
Second place marrow, I'm going home to drink

[Verse 2]
His is the size of a sleeping Labrador
Mine's more a chubby baby in a pram
He shook my hand and said, love, it's the compost
I said, Derek, tell me, what's in your compost

[Pre-Chorus]
He just tapped his nose
And bought me a scone

[Chorus]
Second place marrow, second place me
Red rosette for Derek, blue one for me
Next year I'm digging up the whole of plot three
Second place marrow, Derek, wait and see

[Outro - guitar feedback]
Banana skins and tea
Banana skins and tea
